title: A Surprise at the Bookstore
text: Last Friday, Lucas went into a small bookstore near his apartment. He wanted to buy a book about history. While he was looking at the shelves, he heard someone say his name. He turned around and saw a woman with short hair and big glasses. It was Emma, his best friend from high school! They hadn't seen each other for almost ten years. Emma had moved to another country after school, and slowly they stopped writing to each other. Now she was back in the city for a new job. They were so happy that they forgot about the books. They went for a long walk in the park and talked for three hours. They laughed about their old teachers and shared news about their families. Before they said goodbye, they exchanged phone numbers. This time, they promised to stay in touch.

title: My First Presentation
text: Last week, my teacher gave our class a big task. Everyone had to give a five-minute presentation in front of the class. I chose to talk about my favorite animal, the sea turtle. I found a lot of information and made some simple slides with pictures. The night before, I practiced in front of my cat. She didn't look very interested! The next day, my hands were cold, and my heart was beating fast. When my name was called, I walked to the front of the room slowly. For the first minute, my voice was very quiet. Then I looked at my friend Sara in the second row. She gave me a thumbs up. I relaxed a little and continued. When I finished, my classmates clapped, and some of them asked questions. My teacher said my slides were clear and interesting. After class, I bought myself an ice cream to celebrate.

title: Better Sleep for Nora
text: For many weeks, Nora couldn't sleep well. She went to bed at midnight, but she stayed awake until two or three in the morning. During the day, she felt tired and made small mistakes at work. One day, she read an article about healthy sleep, and she decided to make some changes. First, she stopped drinking coffee after lunch. Then she started going to bed at the same time every night, even on weekends. She also turned off the television and her computer one hour before bed. Instead, she read a book or listened to soft music. The first few nights were not easy. But after two weeks, Nora noticed a big difference. She fell asleep faster and woke up with more energy. Now her friends say she looks happier, and she feels ready for each new day.

title: Three Days Without My Phone
text: On Tuesday morning, I dropped my phone on the kitchen floor. The screen broke into many pieces, and it didn't turn on. The repair shop said I needed to wait three days for a new screen. At first, I was worried. How could I wake up without my alarm? How could I find my way around the city without maps? So I bought a cheap alarm clock and wrote important phone numbers on a piece of paper. On the bus, I didn't look at a screen. Instead, I looked out the window and noticed shops and buildings I had never seen before. At lunch, I talked with my coworkers more than usual. In the evenings, I finished a puzzle I had started months ago. When I got my phone back on Friday, I was happy. But I also decided to use it a little less.
